title: How to hide cursor in Xcode on Mac: Simple Steps for Clean Screen Recordings
metaTitle: How to hide cursor in Xcode on Mac: Quick Guide
description: Learn how to hide cursor on Mac while using Xcode. Since no native toggle exists, discover the best third-party tools and manual workarounds for developers.
targetKeyword: how to hide cursor on mac
intro: There is no built-in, system-wide setting to hide the cursor in Xcode or macOS. To hide your cursor while recording your screen or presenting, you must use a third-party utility like Cursorcerer or manually move the mouse to the edge of your display.
tldr: Xcode lacks a native feature to hide the mouse cursor.
Use third-party apps like Cursorcerer to toggle visibility with a hotkey.
Move your mouse to the far edge of the screen for a temporary fix.
Adjust pointer size in System Settings if visibility is the issue.

blocks.text: Why Xcode Does Not Hide Your Cursor

Apple designs macOS to keep the pointer visible at all times. This ensures you always know where your input focus lies. Because Xcode is a standard macOS application, it follows these system-wide rules. You will not find a checkbox in Xcode settings to make the mouse vanish. Even if you are an app developer using `NSCursor.hide()` in your own code, that only affects the app you are building. It does not change how the Xcode interface behaves while you work.

The most reliable way to hide the cursor is to use a dedicated utility. These apps override the window server to suppress the pointer. Cursorcerer is a popular choice for this task. It runs in the background and listens for a global hotkey. You can set it to hide the cursor immediately or after a short period of inactivity.

items: Download a reputable cursor hiding tool.
Install the app and grant the necessary accessibility permissions.
Open the app settings to define your toggle hotkey.
Use the hotkey to hide or show the cursor while in Xcode.

blocks.text: If you do not want to install extra software, you can move the mouse to the far edge of your screen. This is a common technique for recording short clips. If you have a multi-monitor setup, move the cursor to the corner farthest from your active recording area. This keeps the pointer out of your main workspace.
Some applications force the cursor to reappear if you move the mouse even slightly. If your recording requires absolute stillness, a software utility is much safer than relying on physical placement.
blocks.title: Placement Limitations

blocks.text: Adjusting Pointer Visibility in System Settings

Sometimes you want to hide the cursor because it is distracting or hard to see against a dark Xcode theme. Instead of hiding it, you can change its appearance. Go to System Settings, then Accessibility, then Display. You can change the pointer size or the outline color. This often solves the problem of a distracting cursor without needing to make it disappear entirely.

If your cursor hiding shortcut stops working, check for conflicts. Other apps might have claimed the same key combination. Check your Keyboard Shortcuts settings to see if the hotkey is already in use by another service. Also, ensure your accessibility permissions are still active after a macOS update.

faq.question: Can I hide the cursor inside Xcode settings?
faq.answer: No. Xcode does not have a feature or setting to hide the mouse cursor.

faq.question: Is there a native macOS shortcut to hide the mouse?
faq.answer: No. Apple does not provide a system-wide keyboard shortcut to make the cursor invisible.

faq.question: Will hiding the cursor affect my code?
faq.answer: No. Hiding the cursor is a visual preference and does not change any build settings or code in your project.

steps.name: Download the utility
steps.text: Find a reliable cursor-hiding app online and download the installer to your Mac.

steps.name: Install the app
steps.text: Open the downloaded file and move the application to your Applications folder.

steps.name: Configure accessibility
steps.text: Go to System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility and grant the app permission to control your computer.

steps.name: Set the hotkey
steps.text: Open the app and define a keyboard shortcut to toggle the cursor visibility.

troubleshooting.fix: Check System Settings for conflicting keyboard shortcuts or ensure the app has accessibility permissions.
Ensure no other background apps are forcing the cursor to show when you move the mouse.
